title: Aquatic Monitoring Protocol for Measuring and Collecting Ecological Data
author: Rebecca Hufft
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9j3h4qn
materials: Using the appropriate probes, collect the following data and record on data sheet: a. Temperature (°C)- Use pH probe’s thermometer. b. pH i. Probe should not be allowed to dry out. Store in pH 4 standard (or storage solution if available). ii. If probe does dry out, must soak in standard or storage solution for 1 hour before use. c. Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) d. Dissolved Oxygen (DO, mg/L) i. If the probe has not been used in 7 days, requires 3 minutes to polarize. Turn probe on and wait 3 minutes before testing. ii. Sponge in storage cap must always be moistened (but not soaked) with DI or RO water. e. Electrical Conductivity (EC) f. Flow i. Beginning at thalweg at origin, find a section of reach with uniform bottom and flow. ii. If thalweg is too deep to wade, take measurement at the deepest point possible at the origin and record location on datasheet. iii. Plug cord into back of white unit, zero should appear on screen. iv. To zero counter, switch position up. v. To pause measurements, put switch in middle. vi. To start measuring, put switch down. vii. Use timer to measure flow for 60 seconds at 60% of stream depth. viii. Once back in the office, to calculate surface velocity (m/s), convert the flowmeter readout using the following equation: V(c/m)=(0.000854C)+0.05 g. Rinse all probes with RO water after use and before putting on cap to avoid contamination.

steps.title: Record site location metadata
steps.instruction: Record the survey location using standardized descriptors: country, state (1st political division), county (2nd political division), nearest town or village, directions and distance from that town, any physical landmarks or landscape features, and GPS coordinates with datum and, if possible, uncertainty.

steps.title: Record stream‑reach characteristics
steps.instruction: Document the stream reach characteristics: microhabitats present and their proportion (riffle, pool, run, undercut bank), water condition (murky, clear, foamy), weather from the previous day, water depth at the origin (m), and surface water level at the origin.

steps.title: Collect water quality samples
steps.instruction: At the thalweg (deepest point) adjacent to the transect origin—or at the deepest wadeable point if the thalweg is too deep—collect three CDPHE bottles: Nitrate/Nitrite (250 mL), Total Nitrogen (125 mL), and E. coli (125 mL). Fill each bottle to the max‑fill line, attach the supplied CDPHE label, and complete a CDPHE Request for Analytical Services form for each transect (one form per transect). Each water‑quality test uses its own specific bottle (three bottles per transect). Nutrient bottles contain acid; avoid spilling. Record probe data and the exact sampling location on the datasheet. Samples are time‑sensitive and must be dropped off within 8 hours of collection; no drop‑offs are allowed on Fridays.

steps.title: Measure bank height dimensions
steps.instruction: Measure the following three dimensions for each transect: (1) Total Bank Height – distance from the streambed at the bank edge to the top of the bank; (2) Surface‑to‑bank Height – distance from the water surface level to the top of the bank; (3) Distance to bank from Origin – distance from the origin rebar to the edge of the adjacent stream bank. If water is too deep at the thalweg to wade, take the measurements at the deepest point possible adjacent to the origin and record the location on the datasheet (especially important for dammed reaches).

steps.title: Conduct soil moisture transect
steps.instruction: Lay a 10 m transect perpendicular to the stream bank, starting at 0 m at the bank. At each meter (0 m to 10 m), insert the soil‑moisture meter on the side of the tape that penetrates most easily to a depth of 8 in (20 cm) (full metal length). Record the percent volumetric soil moisture shown on the screen. If the meter takes several minutes to stabilize, wait. Record “W” if the point is under water. Record “Too Rocky” or “TH” if the probe cannot be fully inserted because of rock or hardness. Record “‑‑‑‑” if the screen displays dashes indicating saturation.

steps.title: Kick‑net macroinvertebrate sampling
steps.instruction: Start at the thalweg 20 m downstream from the origin and move upstream toward the origin. Conduct kick‑netting for 1 minute every 5 m, completing 5 sampling bouts per transect (adjust number of bouts if stream sections are dry, keeping samples 5 m apart). At each bout: (a) disturb a 1 m² area upstream of the net with heel or toe to dislodge cobble/gravel and scrape the bed; (b) pick up larger substrate and rub by hand to release organisms; (c) if water is slow, use hands or feet to push material into the net; (d) exclude specimens clinging to the net exterior. Transfer net contents to a mesh bucket: rinse the net exterior to move sediment and specimens to one corner, flip the net inside‑out in the bucket and rinse the outside with water (do not pour water onto the side containing specimens). Continue adding contents along the transect.

steps.title: Preserve macroinvertebrate samples
steps.instruction: Scoop specimens from the mesh bucket into 1 L rectangular Nalgene jars (swirl bucket if needed). Release any fish, amphibians, reptiles, or crayfish back to the stream and note their presence on the datasheet. Fill each jar with no more than 50 % of the sample material; use multiple jars if necessary. Add ethanol to achieve a 50:50 sample‑to‑ethanol ratio. Historically, 2–3 bottles per site (max 5 at TSP or dammed sites) and roughly 2.5 × 750 mL ethanol per day were used. Scrape larger rocks from the bucket to remove attached macroinvertebrates; smaller gravel may be added to the bottle. Label each bottle with an alcohol‑insoluble marker according to the naming‑conventions file. Follow the storage and drop‑off instructions (see next step). Backwash the net with stream water before sampling the next site.

steps.title: Coordinate sample drop‑off with CDPHE
steps.instruction: Water analyses are performed by the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment (CDPHE). Because samples are time‑sensitive, arrange a drop‑off within 8 hours of collection and ensure no drop‑offs occur on Fridays.
